items.name: Tinder
clues: One quick movement of your thumb, again and again. It feels a bit like a game.
Single people, mostly young, who are looking for a date (or just bored on the sofa).
It was launched in 2012 at a start-up event in West Hollywood, California.
Big photos of faces, one at a time, and a small orange-red flame.
Moving a photo to the right means yes. Only when both people say yes can they send messages. Its first name was MatchBox.
Its name is dry material that you use to start a fire.

items.name: Snapchat
clues: Your messages disappear, so you don’t have to think too hard. Streaks make you come back every day.
Teenagers and people in their twenties, mostly sending photos of their faces.
Students at Stanford University in California started it in 2011. Its first name was Picaboo.
Bright yellow, with a white ghost in the middle.
It made funny camera filters famous, like the dog ears and the face swap.
A quick photo plus a word for talking.

items.name: Instagram
clues: Hearts under your photos. You check again and again to see how many you’ve got.
Almost everyone under 40, and every brand, café and influencer in Berlin.
Two founders launched it in San Francisco in 2010. At first it was a check-in app called Burbn.
At the beginning, all the photos were square and had old-fashioned filters. Today the logo is a camera in pink, orange and purple.
In 2012 Facebook bought it for about one billion dollars.
Its name mixes “instant camera” and “telegram”.

items.name: TikTok
clues: Short videos that never stop. You say “one more” and suddenly it’s two in the morning.
Mostly young people, but now also politicians, brands and your aunt.
A Chinese company launched it. In 2018 it joined with Musical.ly, an app for lip-sync videos.
A black background and a white musical note with a red and blue shadow.
Its main page, the “For You” page, chooses videos for you, even from people you don’t follow.
Its name sounds like a clock.

items.name: Netflix
clues: The next episode starts by itself after a few seconds, unless you stop it.
Almost everyone with a sofa and a password, sometimes someone else’s.
It was founded in California in 1997. At first it sent DVDs to people by post.
A black screen, a big red letter, and a short drum sound when it opens.
If you watch for a long time without touching anything, it asks if you are still watching.
“Net” for internet plus a short word for films.

items.name: Spotify
clues: Playlists made just for you, and every December a colourful summary of your year that everyone shares.
Anyone with headphones, from commuters on the U-Bahn to people who run marathons.
Two Swedish entrepreneurs started it in Stockholm in 2006.
Green and black, with a green circle with three curved lines.
One founder misheard a word his partner shouted from another room, searched for it online and found nothing. So they used it as the name.
The music app from Sweden. Some people say its name mixes “spot” and “identify”.
